The CVE: "In JetBrains Kotlin before 2.4.20 code execution was possible via unsafe deserialization in the build cache metadata" - the Kotlin BUILD TOOLING (compiler / Gradle build cache). The NVD's CPE is cpe:2.3:a:jetbrains:kotlin:* for the whole product, so every Kotlin jar matches it, including the runtime libraries.
What this project ships is only runtime libraries, pulled in by OkHttp (the OpenTelemetry OTLP exporter: kotlin-stdlib 2.3.21) and by Spring AI's OpenAI client / okio (kotlin-stdlib 2.3.21, kotlin-stdlib-common 1.9.10, kotlin-reflect 2.3.21). No Kotlin build cache exists at runtime, and nothing here is compiled with Kotlin. Trivy, reading the GitHub advisory for the same CVE, does not flag these jars.
Not "fixed" by raising kotlin.version to 2.4.20: that is a new minor version of a library two third-party clients were built against, to fix code that is not in the jar. Re-check at the expiry, or earlier if Spring Boot moves to Kotlin 2.4.20+ (then this entry is simply unused). Reviewed 2026-09-29, Phase 31; see docs/security.md.

The CVE: "Integer wraparound in IVFFlat index build in pgvector before 0.8.6 allows a database user to write data out-of-bounds ... Only 32-bit systems are affected." That is C code in the PostgreSQL extension (CPE target software: postgresql). com.pgvector:pgvector is the Java client library - a type mapping for the `vector` column - and contains no index code.
The extension itself is not affected either, which was checked on the running catalog-db: `SELECT extversion FROM pg_extension WHERE extname='vector'` = 0.8.6 (the fixed version, image pgvector/pgvector:0.8.6-pg18-trixie), the only vector index is HNSW (idx_product_embedding_hnsw), not IVFFlat, and the host is 64-bit. Reviewed 2026-09-29, Phase 31; see docs/security.md.
